children: ONEOK Inc. (OKE, Financials), the energy infrastructure company, is buying Brazos Midstream's Permian Midland Basin assets for $4.425 billion, but the financing may matter just as much as the acquisition.
Apollo-managed funds will make a $9 billion nonvoting minority equity investment in ONEOK's business.
That money will fund the acquisition while allowing ONEOK to extinguish roughly $5 billion of existing debt.
The structure gives shareholders something unusual: more Permian exposure without issuing common stock, while expected 2027 debt-to-EBITDA falls to roughly 3.25 times.
ONEOK said the Brazos assets should immediately add to earnings and free cash flow per share.

They include about 600,000 dedicated acres under long-term fixed-fee contracts and will more than double ONEOK's Midland Basin processing capacity to approximately 2.3 billion cubic feet per day when projects under construction are included.

Apollo's return is capped at a 7% internal rate of return for the first nine years, which ONEOK says is below its cost of publicly traded equity. The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
Investors will next watch whether the Brazos assets deliver the promised cash-flow growth while ONEOK uses the new structure to reach its leverage target.

title: ONEOK's $4.4 Billion Deal Comes With a $9 Billion Twist
